match.reason: The closest bank point, ecb-business, covers meeting needs and wants and aiming for profit, but it does not teach that some businesses, such as social enterprises, aim to solve a social or environmental problem, and the social enterprise point is too advanced for this course, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: The purposes of business
card: A business is an organisation that makes or sells goods and services. Goods are things you can touch, such as shoes. Services are things done for you, such as a haircut.
One purpose of a business is to provide the goods and services that people want. If nobody wants what it sells, a business will struggle to carry on.
A second purpose is to make a profit for its owners. Profit is the money left over after a business pays its costs from the money it earns.
Some businesses, called social enterprises, also aim to solve a social or environmental problem. A café that trains and hires people who have found it hard to get work is one example.
draft.remember: Businesses provide what people want and aim to make a profit. Some also aim to solve a problem.

a.q: Which of these best describes profit?
opts: Money left over after costs are paid from earnings
All the money a business takes in from its customers
The money an owner puts in to start the business
The money a business pays to its workers each week
a.why: Profit is what remains once the costs are taken out of the money earned. The total money taken in is only the earnings, so it is not profit until costs are paid.
a.clue: Profit is what is left after something is taken away.

b.q: Priya starts a bakery in Bendigo. She sells bread to local families and uses any profit to pay for free lunches at a nearby school. What makes her business a social enterprise?
opts: It also aims to solve a social problem
It sells goods that people can touch
It makes a profit for its owner
It provides what local families want
b.why: A social enterprise also aims to solve a social or environmental problem, and the free school lunches do that. Selling goods people want and making a profit are purposes of all businesses, so they do not set a social enterprise apart.
b.clue: Which purpose do only some businesses have?

a.best: Money left over after costs are paid from earnings

b.best: It also aims to solve a social problem
